concepts.title: Outbreak and Spread of the Revolt
concepts.section: A Mutiny Becomes a Popular Rebellion
concepts.definition: On 10 May 1857 sepoys at Meerut broke out in mutiny over greased cartridges and pay grievances, killed officers and marched to Delhi to proclaim the ageing Bahadur Shah Zafar as emperor; the mutiny became a rebellion as peasants, zamindars and ousted chiefs joined across north India.
concepts.key_idea: Bahadur Shah Zafar's blessing turned a sepoy mutiny into a war with a political head, spreading it along the Ganga valley and central India.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs302.txt Meerut outbreak, Delhi march and spread sections

solution_steps.explain: the mutiny began at Meerut on 10 May 1857
sepoys reached Delhi the next morning and sought Mughal legitimacy
Kanpur, Lucknow, Bareilly and Jhansi became rebel centres

concepts.title: Rumours and Prophecies
concepts.definition: The revolt travelled through rumours - greased cartridges defiling caste, flour kneaded with bone dust, prophecies of British rule ending on the centenary of Plassey - which historians read as expressions of real fears and hopes of a society under rapid change.
concepts.key_idea: Rumour was the rebellion's newspaper: fast, anonymous and believable because it voiced existing anxieties.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs302.txt rumour and prophecy sections and their interpretation
question_patterns: explain the cartridge and flour rumours of 1857

solution_steps.explain: greased cartridges and bone-dust flour spread through cantonments
each rumour encoded real fears of caste pollution and conquest
the Plassey centenary prophecy gave the revolt a destiny narrative

concepts.title: Repression and the Aftermath
concepts.definition: British repression was savage: Delhi was recaptured in September 1857, Bahadur Shah Zafar tried and exiled to Rangoon, rebel villages burnt and sepoys blown from guns; the Government of India Act 1858 transferred rule to the Crown and Queen Victoria's proclamation promised non-interference in religion and an end to annexations.
concepts.key_idea: The revolt's suppression rebuilt the raj: crown rule, army reorganisation and a policy of mistrust toward Indians followed.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs302.txt repression, 1858 act and Queen's proclamation sections

solution_steps.explain: executions, burnings and confiscations followed the recapture of cities
the 1858 act ended company rule and proclaimed crown governance

concepts.title: Visions and Images of the Revolt
concepts.definition: Rebel proclamations like the Azamgarh statement spoke for all communities against the British, while visual records - contemporary sketches, commemorative images of events like theblowing of sepoys - show how both sides remembered 1857; later nationalists recast the revolt as the first war of independence.
concepts.key_idea: Memory of 1857 changed with its readers: loyalist sketches, nationalist celebrations and official histories each built their own rebellion.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs302.txt Azamgarh proclamation, images and nationalist memory sections
question_patterns: what did the Azamgarh proclamation promise and to whom

solution_steps.explain: the Azamgarh declaration addressed Hindus and Muslims jointly against foreign rule
sketches of executions and heroism served each side's memory
twentieth-century nationalists named 1857 the first war of independence

concepts.title: From Outbreak to Proclamation
concepts.definition: The revolt began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut and crown rule was proclaimed through the Government of India Act of 1858; the interval between the two years measures how quickly the raj rebuilt itself after the crisis.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the outbreak year from the act year gives the lag in years.
